methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $302.2B (to $395.7B) × margin 8.0% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $340.6B
K = capital to build it: $302.2B ÷ sales-to-capital 2.93 = $103.1B
σ = 33% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $261.0B
assets in place = NOPAT $0 ÷ WACC = $0; value = ($0 + $261.0B − net debt $17.36B) ÷ 194,049,036 = $1,255.65
inputs: SEC 10-K / 10-Q, trailing four quarters (the main site's reading of the filings)
assumptions: an assumption: the business is riskier than the market sees only through its price
Return on new capital in perpetuity
methods.fit: It is loss-making or growing fast: much of its value is the chance to become a larger, profitable business, which behaves like an option — worth more the more uncertain it is.

methods.formula: Value = D₀ × [(1 + g_L) + H × (g_S − g_L)] ÷ (kₑ − g_L);  growth falls in a straight line from g_S to g_L over 2H years

assumptions: an assumption: dividends rarely grow faster for a decade
methods.fit: It pays a dividend whose growth is likely to slow from today's pace to the economy's, which the H-model spreads over ten years.
